background: Societe Generale is one of France's three largest banks, a universal bank with French retail networks, a large derivatives-driven investment bank, the Ayvens car-leasing business and banking subsidiaries in Africa and Central Europe.
synthesis: Ratings are A+ on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A, with one on a negative outlook, one on a positive outlook and one on a stable outlook, so the three disagree on direction; the last move was a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. The ratios are on the weak side of EU and Nordic peers across the board: CET1 of 13.2% and leverage of 4.3% are both in the bottom quarter, LCR of 146% is below the peer median and NSFR of 115% is in the bottom quarter. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods. The one flagged item, on 29 Jun 2026, is the positive outlook from one of the three; the weakest ratios of the large French banks held here.
